description: Start sending, as the approver of this version: a draft, a paused campaign (resume) or a finished one (after new leads). `revision` is the one check_campaign_launch answered. If the campaign changed since, it answers 409 `campaignChanged` and nothing starts. A blocker answers 409 `campaignNotReady` with the blockers in `details`. When the only blocker is `campaign_limit` (the workspace already runs as many campaigns as it may), it answers 402 `PLAN_GATE` instead, `campaignLimit` (`campaignLimitOver` when more run than the limit allows, `campaignLimitClosed` at a limit of 0), with `limit`, `running` and `upgradeTo` in `details`: pause `running - limit + 1` other campaigns to make room (at a `limit` of 0 no pause makes room, and `upgradeTo` is null: write to hello@colding.app), or read get_billing for how the plan changes. Two launches racing for the last place never both start. A campaign that is already running is never stopped by the limit. Its emails go out under the caller: if the caller loses the `send` permission, or the key is revoked, the campaign pauses as `approval_lapsed`. Launching a running campaign at its current revision changes nothing. An owner may limit the API key you call with: to some mailboxes or campaigns, to outreach or transactional email, and to a number of emails a day or in all. Anything outside those limits answers 403 and nothing is sent: `details.scope` names the limit (`keyMailbox`, `keyCampaign`, `keyStream` or `keyTotal`). When the key has sent all its emails for today, it answers 429 with `details.scope: "keyDay"`, `resetAt` and a Retry-After header. A key can't read or change its own limits: ask a workspace owner. A key launches only a campaign its limits cover whole: the campaign, every mailbox it sends from, outreach, and an email left in its total. Its emails count toward the key's limits, and when an owner narrows the key so it no longer covers the campaign, or its total runs out, the campaign pauses as `approval_lapsed`; when its emails for today run out, the campaign waits for the next day, and get_campaign's `sendingWait` says so. A running campaign can also pause itself, and `pausedReason` says why: `no_mailboxes` (no connected mailbox is left on its list), `no_confirmed_mailboxes` (every mailbox still on its list has an address nobody confirmed; a key with setup permission confirms one with request_mailbox_confirmation and confirm_mailbox_address, otherwise the workspace owner confirms it in the console), `domain_failing`, `approval_lapsed`, `guardrail` (at least 50 of its emails went out in 7 days, and 5% bounced or 0.1% were marked as spam), `list_quality` (its known-invalid share reached 4%; `listGateBreach` has the counts), or `workspace_closing` (the workspace's owner asked to delete it; a launch is refused until they cancel the request). Fix the cause, then launch again. After a guardrail pause the count starts over. If the leads can't be counted, nothing starts and it answers a retryable 503 `leadCountsUnavailable`. With the `validate` permission, a launch also checks the addresses of the leads it hasn't written to yet that have no verdict, or one out of date (`checkLeads`, true by default): each of those leads gets its first email once its check says it may. A lead whose last check got no answer is asked again, which may use another check. `checks` says how many started, or why none did. Launching again with the same approval answers the same checks; a new approval starts new ones. `checkLeads: false` skips only this launch's own checks. While the campaign runs, it still checks up to 50 waiting leads every 15 minutes on its own, as long as whoever launched it holds `validate`, the workspace isn't suspended, its last payment went through and this month has checks left (get_campaign's `leadChecks` says whether it does). While the payment has failed, this launch's own checks wait on hold (`payment_failed`) and start once it goes through. To spend nothing, pause the campaign, or launch it with a key that doesn't hold `validate`.

checkLeads.description: Check the addresses of the leads that have no email from this campaign yet and no verdict, or one out of date, as start_email_checks with campaignId does. A lead whose last check got no answer is asked again, which may use another check. True by default when you hold the validate permission. The launch doesn't wait for them: each lead gets its first email once its address is checked. `checks` in the answer says how many started, or why none did. False skips only this launch's own checks: while the campaign runs, it still checks its waiting leads on its own, as long as whoever launched it holds validate and this month has checks left (get_campaign's `leadChecks`). To spend nothing, pause the campaign, or launch it with a key that doesn't hold validate.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.
